title: Microsoft Purview DLP: DLP event details in Defender alerts through Microsoft Graph
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, permission controls and DLP alert prerequisites are supported. Searches did not find documentation resolving the enrichment's fields, default or separate licensing; minor corrections should add supporting citations and version the example read call.

claims.claim: The feature belongs to Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention and concerns Defender alerts in Microsoft Graph.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Data Loss Prevention – Enrich Defender alerts Graph API with DLP event data

claims.claim: Microsoft plans to enrich the Graph API with DLP event data.
claims.quote: This work enriches the graph API with DLP event data to make correlation and integration easy for customers.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes existing alert data as present in Graph API.
claims.quote: Today alert data is present in Graph API and DLP rule match event details are present in Management API.

claims.claim: Delegated callers need a supported Entra role or qualifying custom role, with Security Reader, Global Reader, Security Operator and Security Administrator supported.
claims.quote: the signed-in user must be assigned a supported Microsoft Entra role or a custom role that grants the permissions required for this operation. ... Security Reader; Global Reader; Security Operator; Security Administrator

claims.claim: No new permission specific to the DLP enrichment is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph DLP alerts enrichment enable default tenant settings permissions content preview. Read List alerts_v2 permissions, SecurityAlert.Read.All and SecurityAlert.ReadWrite.All in the permissions reference, and alert resources. No enrichment-specific permission found.

claims.claim: Viewing DLP alerts in Purview requires a role group listed on the cited DLP alerts page.
claims.quote: If you want to view the DLP alert management dashboard or to edit the alert configuration options in a DLP policy, you must be a member of one of these role groups:

claims.claim: DLP policies must be configured to generate alerts.
claims.quote: Your Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies can be configured to generate alerts when the conditions in a rule are matched. Alerts are configured in DLP policy rules.

claims.claim: Admin consent is reached in Microsoft Entra admin center through Entra ID > Enterprise apps > All applications > application > Security > Permissions > Grant admin consent.
claims.quote: Browse to Entra ID > Enterprise apps > All applications. ... select the application from the search results. ... Select Permissions under Security. ... select Grant admin consent.

claims.claim: POST /v1.0/servicePrincipals/{id}/appRoleAssignments grants an application permission to a client service principal.
claims.quote: App roles that are assigned to service principals are also known as application permissions. ... POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals/9028d19c-26a9-4809-8e3f-20ff73e2d75e/appRoleAssignments

claims.claim: The app role assignment request uses principalId, resourceId and appRoleId, with appRoleId identifying the application permission.
claims.quote: principalId: The id of the client service principal ... resourceId: The id of the resource servicePrincipal (the API) ... appRoleId: The id of the appRole (defined on the resource service principal) to assign to the client service principal.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: SecurityAlert.Read.All grants access across security alert sources rather than being limited to DLP alerts.
claims.quote: Allows the app to read all security alerts, without a signed-in user. ... Allows the app to read all security alerts, on behalf of the signed-in user.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/permissions-reference#securityalertreadall to sources for the statement that alert-read access covers all security alerts rather than DLP alone.

claims.claim: The Graph alerts API includes Microsoft Purview DLP alerts, so its application-permission grants govern access to those alerts.
claims.quote: Alerts from the following security providers are available via these rich alerts and incidents: ... Microsoft Purview Data Loss Prevention
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/graph/api/resources/security-api-overview?view=graph-rest-1.0#alerts to sources for DLP's inclusion among providers of Graph alerts.

claims.claim: No tenant UI or API switch specifically controlling inclusion of DLP event data in Graph alerts is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph DLP alerts enrichment enable default tenant settings permissions content preview; "DLP" "alerts_v2" "enable" "content". Read DLP alerts configuration and Graph alert references. User-based aggregation and Teams export switches govern different features.

claims.where: Scope: Who; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: GET /security/alerts_v2 is the operation used to list Graph security alerts.
claims.quote: GET /security/alerts_v2 ... GET https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/alerts_v2
claims.fix: Replace the two occurrences of GET /security/alerts_v2 with GET /v1.0/security/alerts_v2 to give the documented version explicitly. This versions the existing read operation, not a claim that the enrichment itself is documented in v1.0.

claims.claim: List alerts_v2 supports filtering on serviceSource.
claims.quote: The following properties support $filter : assignedTo, classification, determination, createdDateTime, lastUpdateDateTime, severity, serviceSource and status.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated whether existing callers receive enriched data automatically.
claims.quote: Searched: "DLP" "Graph" "event" "enrich" alerts fields; Microsoft Graph DLP alerts enrichment enable default tenant settings permissions content preview. Read roadmap and beta/v1.0 Graph references; they do not identify the enrichment's rollout behavior or API version.

claims.claim: The described enrichment adds data to a read operation rather than introducing an action operation.
claims.quote: Today alert data is present in Graph API and DLP rule match event details are present in Management API. This work enriches the graph API with DLP event data to make correlation and integration easy for customers.

claims.claim: Alerts may take up to 3 hours to generate after configuring or modifying alerts in a DLP policy.
claims.quote: It may take up to 3 hours to generate alerts after you configure or modify existing alerts in a DLP policy.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not documented whether this enrichment is in v1.0 or only in beta.
